tagline.text: A bridge-linked eco island on Albay Gulf facing Mayon Volcano

location.label: Location
location.text: Bacacay (partly Malilipot), Albay, across the Sula Channel

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,500 (transport, entrance and meals for a day trip, per person)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Bicol International Airport (DRP, in Daraga near Legazpi)

children.text: Cagraray Island lies between Albay Gulf and Lagonoy Gulf, and a bridge over the Sula Channel lets you reach it by road from the mainland. From the hilltop Cagraray Eco Park you can take in the sea, Mayon Volcano and the sunset, and in a single day you can also see the luxury Misibis Bay resort and the Mataas area where prehistoric relics were found.

Cagraray Island sits just off the coast of Albay Province in southeastern Luzon. It borders Albay Gulf, Lagonoy Gulf and the Philippine Sea, and lies between San Miguel Island and Batan Island. Most of its barangays belong to the municipality of Bacacay, while the two barangays of San Antonio and Salvacion belong to neighboring Malilipot. According to Wikipedia the population is about
24,000 people
, living in fishing and farming villages strung along the coast.

The island used to be reachable only by boat or barge, but a bridge now crosses the Sula Channel at its narrowest point, so cars, tricycles and motorcycle taxis (habal-habal) can drive in. From Legazpi, take the road toward Bacacay to Sula village, cross the bridge and the island's hill road begins almost at once. Sources disagree on exactly when the bridge was built, so this guide does not give a year.
The island has three main draws. The first is Cagraray Eco Park, a hilltop park of about
110 hectares

described as the first ecological park in Albay. The second is the luxury Misibis Bay resort on a bay at the far end of the island. The third is archaeology: the Mataas Shell Scoop, a bailer made from a green turban shell and found on this island, was designated a National Cultural Treasure by the National Museum of the Philippines. The island also has Mataas Cave, open to the public and counted among the few show caves in Albay.

It is close enough to Legazpi for a day trip, so it fits easily as an extra day alongside Mayon Volcano and the Cagsawa Ruins. Entry is cheap and the sunsets are known to be lovely, which suits families, couples and groups of friends. Information is not well organized in English or Korean, though, and operating conditions change from year to year, so check the latest announcements before you go.

This hilltop park gives you a wide view of Albay Gulf, nearby islands and, on a clear day, Mayon Volcano. Walking trails have native trees and information signs, and you can also see wind turbines and solar panels, which is where the name "Eco-Energy Park" comes from. Entrance is reported at around

This small chapel stands at the top of the eco park hill. A pilgrim route follows the Stations of the Cross up the slope, and the lookout beside the chapel overlooks the sea toward Misibis Bay. Many visitors come for the view and a rest stop, whatever their faith.

The park's amphitheater is known as a location in the fifth leg of season 4 of The Amazing Race Asia. It is a popular spot for group photos with the sea behind, and it is also used as a stage for local events.
The sunset from the eco park is described as one of the best in Albay. If you settle in around
, you can watch the sea turn red. The park may close early, so check the closing time in advance.

This luxury resort on the island is reported to let non-guests in if they sign up for its eco tour program. It has its own pier, and many guests arrive by motorboat from Legazpi Port. A room costs from about
per night, which is expensive.

blocks.title: Mataas Cave and the Shell Scoop

children.text: The Mataas area has a cave that is open to the public, and a shell scoop radiocarbon-dated to between about 2000 BCE and 300 CE was excavated on the island. Records also say burial jars were found in the island's caves in the 19th century, which makes the island archaeologically important. Check locally whether the cave is open and what guide conditions apply.

blocks.title: Sula Bridge and the Sula Channel

children.text: The bridge linking the mainland to the island is a photo spot in its own right. From the bridge you see the channel and surrounding islands on both sides, and crossing from the Bacacay side gives the feeling of stepping onto an island.
Take a jeepney or van bound for Bacacay from a Legazpi terminal. It takes about
45 minutes to 1 hour
Ride a tricycle from Bacacay to Sula village. It takes about
20 to 30 minutes
Cross the Sula Bridge onto the island, take photos from the bridge, then hire a habal-habal up to the eco park.
After paying the entrance fee, walk the trails and see the amphitheater and the lookout at Stella Maris Chapel.
Eat a packed lunch or snacks and rest in a shaded cottage. Food choices inside the park are limited.
If you booked the Misibis Bay eco tour, see the resort side. Otherwise stroll the village beach and the Mataas area at an easy pace.
If the park is open, watch the sunset, then come down and cross the bridge before dark.
Public transport may stop running early, so settle your return ride in advance.

Bicol is humid all year, but December to May is described as relatively dry and good for outdoor activities. Bacacay's average temperature is roughly
and its annual rainfall is reported at about 1,732 mm.

Bicol lies in the typhoon belt, so in the rainy and typhoon seasons the sea can turn rough and boats may stop running. Check the weather and port announcements before you leave, and go early in the morning or late in the afternoon to avoid the heat and get better photos.

If you stay on the island, the best-known choice is the Misibis Bay resort. It is a luxury resort with high prices, so to save money it is more realistic to base yourself in Legazpi or Tabaco and visit as a day trip. Legazpi has hotels and guesthouses at every price level and is close to the airport.

Restaurants are few around the island and the park. The eco park may sell simple snacks, but choices are limited, so bring water, snacks and a packed lunch. In Bacacay town and the coastal villages you can try seafood such as grilled fish, shrimp and squid, along with Bicol local dishes. Bicol dishes made with coconut milk and chili are easier to find in Legazpi restaurants, so having a solid meal in the city before you head to the island is one option. Restaurants on the island may close early, so it is safest to plan your meals around lunchtime.
Bring plenty of cash. Entrance fees, motorcycle taxis and snacks are easiest to pay in cash, and ATMs may be hard to find on the island, so withdraw money in Legazpi beforehand.
Going early in the morning or late in the afternoon avoids the heat and gives better light for photos.
Bring water, snacks, sunscreen, a power bank and a trash bag. Take your trash back with you.
If you travel by public transport, check the last return ride in Sula village in advance.
Agree on the fare before boarding a habal-habal or tricycle, and if you want a round trip, agree on the waiting time too.
If you want the Misibis Bay eco tour, ask the resort ahead of time. Conditions for visitors change often.
The view of Mayon Volcano is best early in the morning when there are fewer clouds.
If you want to see Mataas Cave, go with a local guide and ask at the local barangay whether it is open.
In the rainy and typhoon seasons boats can stop running and some roads can flood. Always check the weather and the latest announcements before you leave.
The eco park's entrance fee and hours differ by source (for example 6 AM to 6 PM or 8 AM to 5 PM), so confirm them locally.
Paid adventure activities such as the zipline and wall climbing have been suspended since COVID. Check whether they are running before you visit.
Some roads inside the island are rough and have few streetlights, so getting around is awkward after dark.
At caves and archaeological sites, do not touch or take any relics, and follow the residents' guidance.
Shops and medical facilities can be hard to find on the island. Prepare medicines and personal items in Legazpi beforehand.

A volcano famous for its near-perfect cone, visible in the distance even from the eco park lookout.
Ruins where a church bell tower buried by the 1814 eruption still stands, famous for photos with Mayon Volcano behind it.
A coastal city north of Bacacay and a gateway toward the island. You can enjoy coastal scenery on the way toward the island.
